Name:  ___                     Unit No:   ___

Chief Complaint:
Abdominal pain, N/V/diarrhea
 
Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure:
none
 
History of Present Illness:
___ with PMH of DMI, chronic pancreatitis, chronic abdominal 
pain, asthma, and urinary retention presenting with one day of 
nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Patient reports she felt in her 
usual state of health until two days prior to admission when she 
developed the acute onset of profuse diarrhea. She had 
""countless"" episodes of diarrhea overnight on ___, and the 
following morning developed nausea and vomiting and a subjective 
fever. She called her PCP and was referred to the emergency 
room. She denies recent sick contacts, change in diet, or 
travel. No melena, hematochezia, or hematemesis. She endorses 
crampy abdominal pain preceding her first bout of diarrhea, 
followed by severe abdominal pain in the epigastrium radiating 
in a band like pattern across her abdomen, consistent with her 
chronic abdominal pain. No chest pain, shortness of breath, 
lightheadedness, dizziness, or syncope.

While in the emergency room she received Dilaudid 0.5mg IV x 4 
and 1.0mg x 1, as well as Benadryl, Zofran, and IV fluids. She 
had persistently low blood sugars ranging from 66-106 and 
received ___ amp of D50 twice. She was then admitted to the 
medical service.  
 
Past Medical History:
#. Type I DM (since age ___, c/b severe gastroparesis)  
#. Chronic pancreatitis  
#. Chronic abdominal pain  
- unclear etiology likely multifactorial ___ chronic 
pancreatitis, gastroparesis and psychosocial factors  
#. H/o PUD secondary to H. pylori  
#. Gastritis  
#. Iron deficiency anemia  
#. Right adnexal cyst  
#. Status post cholecystectomy (___)  
#. Asthma  
#. Urinary retention (worsened by diphenhydramine and narcotics  

previously)
#. H/o line infections  
#. Depression & borderline personality disorder; h/o cutting  
behavior and SA but none > ___ year.

___
Family History:
Grandmother, uncle and mother with DM. GM with pacemaker. 
History of hypertension.

4. Depression and anxiety: Well controlled with regimen of

and nausea. Goal of 50cc/hr reached and she was sent home

Discharge Diagnosis:
viral gastroenteritis exacerbating chronic pancreatitis with 
abdominal pain and diabetes type one with gastroparesis
chronic abdominal pain
Depression, Anxiety
 
Discharge Condition:
Mental Status:Clear and coherent
Level of Consciousness:Alert and interactive
Activity Status:Ambulatory - Independent

 
Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted with probable gastroenteritis.  This resolved 
with conservative management.  You were begun on tube feeds and 
tolerated this to between 30 to 50cc/hr. Your were given low 
dose narcotic pain meds and this was weaned down although you 
still required some dilaud towards the end of the stay.  You 
agreed not to take other narcotic pain meds at home except for 
significant pain, and you had your tramadol discontinued in the 
hospital (given you refused it when offered over several days).  
Your insulin was decreased given your initial decrease in diet 
and adjusted as needed.  As per past hospitalizations, you did 
not initially allow ___ docs to see you, but they did leave 
recommendations after seeing you on the last few days.  You will 
need to resume your outpatient Insulin regimen and follow it as 
you normally do with your doctors.   Your PCP is currently on 
vacation, but Dr. ___ Dr. ___ aware of your 
hospitalization.  Please follow up with your PCP.
